Across hardwood never seen

Grew sapling apple trees

That you last saw

In endless fall

And only touched by green,

Speckling the autumn sea,

Crests and breaks in the breeze,

Swallowing cold from tender feet.

.

Windows made of two-way glass

Start to skew the scenes that last

And perhaps to child’s eyes,

Brought that cup of sapphire,

Sweet relief, now to realize

Those panes rose through fire.

.

And when you could climb the hillside

O how many treasures you knew to find:

A seafloor bathed in pale morning light-

A twin-suited room, wherein we might

find youth suspended forever in midair,

Still, to count each strand of hair

And drag fingers across the swells residing there-

An atrium, small, where many have and will have slept

Yet whose magic, in one child’s heart, is forever kept-

The very room the coddled your heavy head

Despite the half constructed armada beneath the bed.

.

And from just below crept thick, welcomed haze

Saturated the the savory scents of holidays,

And lightly mixed with familiar must,

But tempting enough to make small footsteps rush

Down from their perches upon branches and lofts-

Like the squirrels they would chase, though had never caught-

And upon entering, let aromas lick the tip of each nose

To melt away the dusting of pink rose

With onions stewing in great, cream-filled bowls

As the conversations grow to a passionate roar,

Joining the phantom echoes resonating between the floors-

Echoes which the children will largely ignore,

To listen to the jolly man sing at the door,

Or touch the red fuzz on the adjacent room’s floor,

Or eat the minimal amount of food off their plates

That will earn two peanut butter kandy-kakes.

.

Not all nights are full, and on those when all are tired,

Authentic red-roof pizza is all to be desired.

No matter how frivolous or dire a night’s activities,

There will always be safe haven under pine titan canopies.

While honeysuckle may wilt, and towers we scaled are felled,

lingering sweetness, and desire to reach higher will always serve well.

.

Over many more rivers,

Through many more woods,

To many more houses we go,

And even more next year,

And still more the next-

Large as those titans shall we grow.

.

.

The spoiler markup on R****t abuses Markdown link syntax because it's a Javascript hack that uses the action of visiting a link as a trigger to modify the page. It's not surprising that putting links inside a link makes the Markdown parser barf. I understand being compatible with published vanilla Markdown as far as possible, and I even understand being backward compatible with that other site, but maybe Voat should use a different syntax for spoiler boxes.

abuses Markdown link syntax because it's a Javascript hack that uses the action of visiting a link as a trigger to modify the page

?? Not true at all. Reddit has no standard spoiler syntax, nor is JavaScript involved. All subreddits that implement the [Spoiler](/s "Spoiler here") syntax use the CSS ::after pseudo-element and content: attr(title), which is the same trick used here, only it's part of the default stylesheet.

The syntax is not used only for familiarity, but because there is no tag meant for spoilers in HTML. Since Voat uses an external library for Markdown (MarkdownDeep), they are disinclined to adding non-standard syntax to the parser.

As for the parser barfing, even if it didn't, nested links are impossible in HTML in the first place, e.g.:

<a href="http://voat.co">The outside link <a href="http://google.com">(this inside link goes to Google)</a> goes to Voat.</a>

is impossible because the first </a> will close the first link, forcing the second one to also close, leaving the last part ("goes to Voat") unlinked. If the parser did not barf, it would instead reveal part of the spoiler text.

All that said, yes, we could think of a new spoiler syntax, but it will a be very low priority feature and require either tacking on in front of the parser (ugly, like how @username mentions are implemented) or patching MarkdownDeep (which they probably will not accept).

Patches are welcome on Github, or ideas if you can think of a good syntax.

Personally I would use strikethroughs, but strikethroughs are not in standard Markdown either.

Oh, I agree that this is a low-priority problem. That's especially true if Voat is just using a third-party Markdown parser; the existing fragmentation of Markdown is bad enough without adding to it unnecessarily. Most of that fragmentation, of course centers on abuses of Markdown link syntax like the ones we use here for spoilers and inline images. There's also an underlying problem that Markdown's link syntax is complete dogshit; compare it to BBCode or MediaWiki markup, both of which manage to do things better with half the complexity.

However, the abuse of the link syntax is only there because the spoiler markup uses an URL fragment as a hack to change display of the page; we could just as easily use spoiler markup that required the reader to highlight spoiler text manually, or toggle a button. None of those is ideal, none of them is a high priority, but both of them would avoid confusing the Markdown parser, so they would avoid breaking links.

a hack to change display of the page; we could just as easily use spoiler markup that required the reader to highlight spoiler text manually, or toggle a button.

One thing. I think you're confusing something here. The display is merely CSS and not related to the syntax/markup, and the other solutions you mention can all be done with the same syntax/markup but different CSS. The "URL fragment" (i.e. the fact that it is using the link syntax or <a> tag) has nothing to do with the display or changing the display.

  • e.g. you can make [Spoiler](/s "Luke's father") show "Luke's father" in white-on-white and require highlighting to reveal the text. Using only CSS.

  • Conversely you can also make *Luke's father*, which results in <em>Luke's father</em> show the text "Spoiler" and require a hover to reveal (exactly the same behaviour as current implementation on Voat). Again using only CSS.

Syntax/markup and display/CSS are completely independent. You need to separate the issues -- you want the syntax changed (and I agree). Don't lump it together with an issue with the display or its implementation, as it is not even an issue, and it can be changed per subverse with CSS (one subverse can have hover to display, one subverse can have highlight to display, etc). It makes it very difficult to talk about issues otherwise.

Sorry if this comes across harshly; I am writing in a hurry.

Well, I haven't looked at all at the way spoiler markup is implemented, so it is fine for you to tell me - not to mention that the site keeps going up and down every time I try to load comments; no doubt it is doing the same for you.. Yes, there are really two different issues, so I'm sorry if my posting has caused them to get mixed together. The one that really matters is that it ought to be possible to place any sort of text inside spoiler markup and have it function as intended. If that's just a problem with a third-party component, it may be a very low priority to fix; in that case it ought to be documented at least.
